lead: Nevada plumbing deals with very hard water, desert heat and slab homes, plus real winters around Reno. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers from Las Vegas to Reno.
risk: very hard water scale, slab leaks and frozen pipes in Northern Nevada
risk_short: hard water, slab leaks and frozen pipes
why: Southern Nevada's water is very hard, so scale builds up in water heaters, tankless units, faucets and showerheads. Most Las Vegas homes are built on slabs, with supply lines under the floor that can leak. Water conservation is a priority in the desert.
Reno, Carson City and the high desert see hard freezes, and pipes on outside walls and in crawl spaces freeze. Nevada licenses plumbing contractors through the Nevada State Contractors Board.
problems: Las Vegas, Henderson and North Las Vegas
Reno, Carson City and the high desert
tips: Flush your water heater yearly to clear scale.
Watch your water bill for signs of a slab leak.
Wrap outdoor pipes in Northern Nevada before winter.
areas: Calls come from Las Vegas, Henderson, North Las Vegas, Reno, Sparks, Carson City and rural Nevada.

faq.q: Why is Las Vegas water so hard?
faq.a: Southern Nevada's water picks up calcium and magnesium on its way through the Colorado River system. That hardness leaves white scale on fixtures and in water heaters. A softener and regular flushing help.
